entries.title: Orbit Dash - Orrery
entries.summary: Rebuilt as an 18th-century brass orrery printed on cyanotype paper. The last of the catalogue reworks.

sections.heading: New direction
items: The neon-on-black space look is gone. The whole game is now engraved line work on a hand-coated cyanotype plate - graduated tracks with degree ticks, a toothed brass sun gear, and an engraved star chart turning slowly behind the mechanism.
Colour carries the rules and nothing else: brass is you and only you, copper is lethal and only lethal, verdigris is reward, and every cool blue line is scenery.
No bloom and no film grade - filmic post would turn engraved line work to mush. Only paper grain and a plate vignette, because those are the medium rather than an effect.

sections.heading: New play
items: Three tracks instead of two, still on one button - a tap steps you outward and wraps around.
Gates: verdigris arcs to thread for a chain multiplier that bleeds away if you stop threading.
The mainspring, wound by threading gates. Hold the button to spend it and the entire machine slows, letting you shatter debris instead of dodging it.
Threaded gates stamp tick marks on the plate and wrecks leave ink blots, so a long run visibly accumulates evidence on the paper.

sections.heading: Fair by construction
items: Debris can never share a bearing with other debris, so exactly one track is ever blocked at a given angle. Staying put survives if it is not your track; one tap survives if it is, and the tap always lands you somewhere guaranteed clear.
Because every piece of debris drifts at the same rate, the gaps between them never change - the check at spawn time holds for the whole run.
Verified: 900 frames with zero shared-bearing violations, and a reactive player survived a 30-second run without dying.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Fixed a crash on load where the first resize ran before the paper buffer existed.
Guarded the zero-size layout pass that could collapse the canvas and spawn everything at the origin.
Track changes are now snappy enough to finish well inside the guaranteed clearance arc.

entries.title: Hardburn
entries.summary: New game. You launch a missile, then you have to fly it.

sections.heading: Three directions, and the gaps between them
items: Aim is where the mouse points. Airframe is where the nose points, which is where thrust goes. Flight path is where you are actually going - and it turns amber when it stops agreeing with your aim.
Swing the nose 90 degrees off your flight path and you can thrust sideways out of a corner; swing it all the way round and you retro-burn while still looking where you are going.
Hold the motor and it burns; let go and you are a dart with gravity attached. A nose-fired grapple carves the turns the airframe cannot.

sections.heading: Scoring and courses
items: Style scoring: thread gates near centre, skim within 8m of a surface, load the airframe in hard turns, and swing off a hooked surface.
Only the improvement over your personal best on a course banks at full rate, so grinding is not a strategy - flying better is.
Courses are seeded and generated: type any word and you get that course, forever, identically, on any machine. Four difficulties from Milk Run to Suicidal.

sections.heading: Airframes
items: 23 across six rarities. From Rare up the airframe is genuinely rebuilt rather than recoloured - length, calibre, nose, fins, canards and pods all change, and the hangar preview is the mesh that launches.
Epic and above carry a sixth system on Q; Legendary and Mythic bring Rewind, Singularity, Nova Lance, Event Horizon and Ascension.
Bone-on-ink monochrome world, with saturated colour reserved for your missile and its exhaust - so rarity is literally how much colour is on screen.

entries.title: Rats With Wings
entries.summary: New game. A 3D pigeon simulator about being a small grey menace.

sections.heading: The plaza
items: 120 seconds and a limited payload. Bomb pedestrians from above - head hits score double, and they have opinions about it.
Desecrate the bronze General for a fortune, dive-bomb people to snatch their ice cream mid-lick, and set off car alarms for no reason at all.
Eating refills your ammunition, fast hits chain a five-times chaos multiplier, and cooing summons the local flock to follow you around like a tiny feathered gang.

sections.heading: Consequences
items: Hit the hot dog cart and the vendor starts hurling buns at you - a problem, right up until you realise the ones he misses with are free food.
Your splats stay on the pavement and in people's hair for the rest of the round, so the plaza slowly fills with evidence.
Ranks run from Sidewalk Nobody to Flying Rat Supreme.

entries.title: Echoes v2.0
entries.summary: A complete rebuild, written from scratch rather than evolved. Three new tracks.

sections.heading: Two senses, sharpened
items: The central tension is now explicit: the lamp shows the truth, the echo shows memory.

The echo is a real expanding wavefront, not a screen effect. Rays are cast at fire time and each return is held until the wave physically reaches it, so returns arrive near-to-far. Brightness falls with range and with how square-on the surface is - walls you face light up, walls you skim stay dark.
Phosphor shows where a wall was, not what has moved since. The lamp burns the cell, and anything with eyes can see you holding it.

sections.heading: New tracks
items: The Drowned Floor - the Tenant returns nothing on sonar, a moving hole in your picture, and only advances while the lamp is off it. Open three sluices while the flood rises.

The Chorus - seven identical bowed figures, six recordings and one that is not. Ping them and the live one burns a white outline into the phosphor permanently; or spend cell, because under lamplight the recordings carry tape dropout. Information costs either noise or power.
The Transmitter - the Needle is deaf to light and hunts sound only. Carry the accumulator to the array; hands full means no ping and no sprint.

sections.heading: Presentation
items: Procedural materials baked per track, real lighting with actual penumbra from three offset origins, and water as a marching-squares contour so the shoreline cuts diagonally across the grid instead of following it.

Creatures built on real top-down anatomy - you see crowns of heads and tops of shoulders, never faces, and tell them apart by silhouette alone. You are now a person, with the lamp held out in front where the beam actually comes from.
The room cuts to silence for about 270ms before every scare hit, then swells back. That gap does most of the work.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Screen shake could run away on Track 03 and throw the camera thousands of pixels off-screen; it is now hard-capped globally.
The Needle could never actually kill you - it halted 42px short of its target while its kill radius was 30px.
The struggle QTE was unwinnable: the meter clamped at exactly 1.0, but decay was applied before the win check.

entries.title: Abyssal Dredging - rework
entries.summary: The interface folds away and there is now an actual ocean under the rig.

sections.heading: The panels
items: The old layout hard-split the page: the rig got a strip at the top, a static panel took the rest, and nothing could be moved or hidden.
Four independent docks - Upgrades, Cargo Hold, Extraction Log and Console - each folding to a thin labelled tab on the screen edge.
Focus mode folds all four at once, leaving nothing on screen but the sea. Phones start folded, so a first-time player lands on the water instead of behind a drawer.

sections.heading: The ocean
items: Previously the cable dropped off the bottom of the rig strip and the haul only ever appeared as text in a list. Now there is a real water column and the net travels down into it.

Above water: storm sky with parallax cloud bands, rain as real streaks that punch ripple rings into the surface, branching lightning, and a jack-up rig drawn in full - lattice legs, derrick A-frame, turning sheave, and a sodium lamp with a feathered cone. The submerged legs are drawn before the water, so the rig stands in the ocean rather than on it.

Below water: a depth-graded column down to true black, marine snow in three parallax layers, drifting jellyfish, a sunken salvage field silhouetted against backscatter murk, and a leviathan that crosses the deep every minute or two.

sections.heading: One gameplay change
items: The loot roll now happens at the bottom of the dive rather than at the end, so the catch physically rides up through the water - each item a seeded silhouette rim-lit in its rarity colour, with the net glowing in the colour of the best item in the bag. You read the result off the ocean before the log tells you.
No balance was touched: every drop chance, upgrade cost, multiplier, max level, crush yield and rank threshold is byte-identical to the original.

sections.heading: Settings and fixes
items: Auto-scrap now covers the full ladder, with a warning on anything from Legendary up because it can eat a one-in-fifty-million pull. The cutscene fires and the Collection records the discovery before the crush, so you keep the reveal and the completion credit.
Cutscene skipping is now a per-tier threshold instead of a single on/off, and old saves migrate automatically.
Fixed the cursor vanishing during cutscenes, so you could not see what you were aiming at to hit Skip, and hero text overflowing narrow windows.

entries.title: Sole & Co. - update
entries.summary: Two pieces of playtest feedback: it was too hard, and the shoes all looked identical.

sections.heading: Difficulty - it was a bug, not a preference
items: The root cause was an economy bug. Wholesale asks averaged 0.93x a shoe's value and customer offers averaged 0.94x, so the average trade lost money before rent was even deducted.
Starting cash $1,500 to $2,400, display slots 8 to 10, customer budgets $90-180 to $170-330 with a 22% chance of a whale, and patience 13s to 24s.
Rent down from $130 + $14/day to $95 + $8/day, offers up across every tier, and haggle success from 50% to 62%.
Verified over 2,800 simulated flips: buying at or under 0.75x value and selling to a matching customer now clears about 173% margin, versus roughly break-even before.

sections.heading: The shoes
items: Nine models to twelve, and one shared sole becomes six sole architectures - cup, vulc, air, boost, stack and wedge - each with its own outsole tread.
The big 'they all look identical' tell was the heel line: it sat at about 88% of collar height on every model, rounding every back into the same pod shape. Now derived per model at 60-76%.

The ankle opening is a real cut now - a closed dark band generated from the rim curve with a padded lip - instead of a floating line, and the thick stroked collar band that read as a roll bar is gone.
15 to 17 colourways rebuilt for contrast, and fixed a colour-role collision that was painting orange toe bumpers onto a Converse.

sections.heading: Known limitation
items: At large scale these read as good vector illustrations rather than photoreal sneakers. The one thing that measurably worked was measuring against a reference photo, which corrected proportions three prior passes had guessed wrong.

entries.title: Redwater - A Frontier Tale
entries.summary: Replaces the old Blue Lock game entirely. A top-down open-world western RPG in a single file.

sections.heading: The county
items: Six thousand acres of bleached flats, red mesa and dry riverbed, drawn like a spaghetti western printed on an 1880s wanted poster - flat lithographic shapes, heavy blacks, one low raking sun that swings through a seven-minute day.
Twelve named places including the town of Redwater, the outlaw hold at Black Mesa, Copper Creek Mine, Hargrave Ranch, Perdition Depot, Boot Hill and the Old Mission.

Eight buildings you walk into rather than menus that open - the Dry Gulch saloon with a piano man who only knows one tune, the sheriff's office with a prisoner who swears he was nowhere near that horse.

sections.heading: No side, then a side
items: You start as a drifter nobody has decided about. Sheriff Abel Cordell offers tin; Silas Kane offers the other thing.

Both branches have their own chain of work - bounties, a stagecoach to hold, a raid on the mesa, or a bank to crack and a sheriff to hang - and both converge on Augustus Hargrave, the baron paying both sides of every argument in the county.
When the story runs out, the bounty board and the job board keep printing paper forever.

sections.heading: Twenty guns, four that wake up
items: Common iron is pale and worn and does nothing but fire; fine steel is blued and brass-banded; rare arms carry an ability on Q.

Four legendaries carry an awakening on F that charges as you deal damage: Dead Man's Hand stops time and marks every soul in sight, Judgment lays four expanding rings of fire the ground remembers, Widowmaker drains the world to ink and bone for one shot, and Iron Horse brings six barrels and ghost horses through the smoke.

sections.heading: Also in there
items: Dead Eye slow-motion aiming, dive-rolls, horses you can buy or break in, and dynamite.
A wanted level that sends posses after you, quick-draw duels on a full cinematic screen, ten perks, and a save that keeps your ride.

entries.title: Meridian - release notes
entries.summary: Rivalforge is now Meridian, moved from a night-shift machine hall to a daylit one.

sections.heading: Renamed and relit
items: The old name described a dark room the game no longer has. A meridian is both high noon and the precision line on a transit instrument.

Re-authored world materials, environment map, light rig (the key is now the warm one, the fill the cool one), volumetrics, post grade, and a full light-mode flip of the interface. The forge became a sun gate - a glimpse, not a wall.
The file is still rivalforge.html and saves still live under the old key, deliberately: renaming either would wipe every player's inventory.

sections.heading: Two new rarity tiers
items: Forged - finishes that react to the game. Overclock reads your magazine and runs cold blue to hot orange as it empties; Parallax windmills the Longbow's scope collars and locks as the rifle settles; Filament charges as the balisong closes.

Zenith - finishes that perform, with their own animations, one per weapon: Aperture (karambit drawn out of a portal), Teardown (rifle hangs in eighteen pieces and assembles on the draw), Afterimage, Glitch, Swarm, Tourbillon (a working clock on the receiver, and nine more behind it that all disagree) and Phase.
Total skins now 59.

sections.heading: Economy rework
items: The old odds mirrored CS:GO, which without a cash market behind them was punishing - a crate returned 5-13% of its price and three of the four crates could not drop the top two tiers at all.
Crate price now buys genuinely better odds: Classified-or-better runs 5.8%, 10.7%, 16.6% then 25% up the ladder, with expected return a consistent 60-78%.
Every crate can produce every tier, and Forged and Zenith come from a shared pool.

New Calibration: a tolerance-drift gauge fills on every disappointing open and guarantees a Classified or better when it fills, with five purchasable levels to shorten it. The first credit sink that is not itself a gamble.
Trade-up is now five items instead of ten.

sections.heading: Weapons, interface and performance
items: Melee rewritten - swings were one symmetric arc that read like a windscreen wiper, now proper keyframed routines with wind-up, fast strike, overshoot and slow recovery.

Fixed the hand freezing after an inspect, the karambit being held blade-up, inspect dropping your hand below where it belongs, and the Hornet's reflex sight having a solid block in the bore - the SMG could not be aimed for the entire life of the build.
Rebuilt the type ladder against measured contrast; the bright rework had left micro-labels at 2.6:1 and a Forged skin's name at 1.57:1.
Fixed a ghost-mesh leak on weapon switches (19ms to 8ms) and Tourbillon's 46ms first-frame hitch.

entries.title: Aura Fighters - rework
entries.summary: Every form now plays differently, and rivals became four real archetypes.

sections.heading: Combat
items: All 11 forms shared one melee behaviour and the specials collapsed into 6 types - beam alone covered 4 forms. Now every form owns a unique melee signature, ki blast and special.

Signatures include a 3-hit launcher, 5-hit chain lightning, a blink strike with a delayed echo, i-frame slips, a single shockwave slam with no combo, Rend-stacking claws that detonate, Heat that accelerates then overheats, Seal marks every third hit, strikes that drag enemies in, and a 360-degree omni-strike.
New systems: Rend bleed stacks, Heat redline, Seals that amplify Execution, and i-frames.
Three distinct beams rather than four copies of one, with a rebuilt renderer - hot core, stepped falloff, muzzle charge sphere and impact blooms that terminate on the target.

sections.heading: Enemies
items: Rivals used to run one behaviour with scaled stats. Four archetypes now: Rusher (telegraphed lunges, long recovery), Zoner (holds range, bursts you off when you close), Duelist (circles and counters mid-attack) and Warlord (blinks in, area slams, enrages below 40%).
Every attack is telegraphed with a closing ring and threat cone. Interrupting one means landing your combo finisher early in the tell - a read, not a mash.

sections.heading: Progression and visuals
items: Enemy lap scaling cut from 1.55x to 1.32x and the Zenkai floor raised. The old curve punished skill - clean clears grew you 1.17x per lap against enemies growing 1.55x. Clean play now keeps pace indefinitely.
New title scene with a live attract shot, particle-driven auras unique to each form, per-transformation outfits, enemy tier crests, persistent scorch decals and a rebuilt angular HUD.

sections.heading: Performance and fixes
items: 223ms to roughly 3.4ms per frame, about 65x faster - soft particles blit from a sprite cache instead of rebuilding radial gradients every frame, plus off-screen culling.
Fixed a permanent soft-lock where a trimmed beam projectile could lock you out of every action forever.
Fixed stun-lock from fast forms, Ultra being effectively invulnerable (11 i-frames on a 5-frame cooldown), and a safe zone where enemies ignored you past 600 units so you could charge ki for free.

entries.title: Flytale v3
entries.summary: A real 1-bit pixel art pass, and roughly double the length.

sections.heading: Art - the watercolour fix
items: Every soft edge came from four things: anti-aliased arc() circles, ctx.rotate(), rgba() alpha and browser text. All four are gone - discs are integer scanlines, rotation is nearest-neighbour pre-baked in 16 steps, transparency is checkerboard dither, and text is thresholded to 1-bit.
Sprites are now built on a real pixel grid with a hard 1px black outline on every shape, in a fixed 28-colour palette.
The spider's legs were drawn in the same purple as its body and underneath it, so they rendered as nothing. Rebuilt at 78x56 with long two-segment legs, knees above the body, eight eyes and fangs.
Fixed the zapper racket rendering as a magenta blob, and the electric arc drawing as a wall instead of a bolt.

sections.heading: Length
items: Roughly doubled, to six chapters: the sink, the ant picket line, an early ambush where you can only survive the man, the moth at the hall lamp, the spider's toll booth, then the kitchen.
He now has 8 weapons before his bare hands - flyswatter, newspaper, bug spray, zapper racket, vacuum, shotgun, flamethrower and rocket launcher.
Verified with a full automated playthrough: all six chapters and all nine weapon stages reach an ending, with no errors.

entries.title: Multiverse Fighters - rework
entries.summary: Real animation, real opponents, and a camera that follows the fight.

sections.heading: Animation
items: Knee direction fix - every knee value was positive, so legs bent forward and the run read as backwards.
Proper gait: thigh swings fore and aft, knee tucks on the rear swing, arms counter-swing, two bobs per cycle.
Attacks went from 3 phases to 4 - anticipate, snap, follow-through, settle - with the overshoot extrapolated from the windup-to-strike vector, so every attack got it without new poses.
Motion smear trails, squash and stretch on takeoff, landing and strike frames, secondary motion on hair and cape, and root motion so attacks step into the hit.

sections.heading: Movement and ultimates
items: Momentum-based instead of lerp-to-target, with 23% higher top speed and heavier gravity.
Double jump with a flip, aimable air dash, fast fall, skid on hard reversals, and a dash attack that keeps momentum. Jump moved to Space so W and S could become aim directions.

12 unique charge stances and 12 unique charge routines - all 12 previously used the same arms-back pose and identical converging orbs. Per-ultimate camera: Vanta charges near-black, Ronin desaturated and near-frozen.

sections.heading: Opponents and camera
items: The dummy became five levels: Dummy, Rookie, Fighter, Veteran, Master. The AI runs your exact code, so it cannot do anything you cannot.
A real brain: approach, retreat, guard, anti-air, dash-in, zoning, low pokes, jump-ins and specials, reacting to your swings and turtling when low.
You now have HP, hitstun, blocking at 84% reduction, K.O. with slow-motion, round reset and a win tally.
The camera was locked wide; it now tracks the midpoint and zooms on separation, with zoom kick on heavies, pullback for ultimates and a snap to the loser on K.O., plus real parallax.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Tornado and Supernova left the player hovering after the ult, and the viewport reported 0 during layout so a window resize mid-fight never recovered.
Redrew Aegis's shield - the concentric-disc-with-a-star read as a real trademarked design, and is now an original heater shield with a chevron band.

entries.title: Grand Line - Sea of Fruits
entries.summary: Rebuilt as a top-down pirate action-RPG, drawn like a woodblock adventure print.

sections.heading: Content
items: Four Devil Fruits with three abilities each - Flame, Ice, Rumble and Quake. Swap freely; bosses drop theirs and wild fruits wash up on the islands.
Five islands to clear, from Dawn Shore to the Volcano Crown, each with its own enemies, a named boss and a recommended level.
Open sea sailing - walk into the water and you board your boat. Something lives out in the deep.
A running voyage objective, a compass that points the way, and a chart of the whole world.

sections.heading: Feel
items: Cutlass combos, i-frame dashes, hitstop and screen shake.
Enemies telegraph, circle, and break off if you outrun them.
Levels, Beli, bounties, and a Quake ultimate that lands on hand-cut impact frames.

sections.heading: Art
items: Flat inked shapes, carved waves and a parchment interface, with powers that detonate as bursts of raw pigment.

entries.title: Rank Zero - Sovereign Protocol
entries.summary: Rebuilt from the ground up, with its own name and world.

sections.heading: Identity
items: The System is now the Lattice, hunters are delvers, gates are rifts, and the nine Monarchs are the nine Sovereigns. Bosses, weapons and armour renamed to match.
Added a proper title screen.

sections.heading: A new look - The Gilded Ledger
items: The arena is a book left open: a repeating codex page with ruled lines, columns of writing, margins, corner lozenges, folio numbers and your rift's grade illuminated under the floor.
Gold is the Lattice, red is anything that can hurt you, and every kill leaves a blot of ink that stays on the page.
New typeface, new palette, rebuilt HUD, and an illuminated ledger for the hub.

sections.heading: The live grade
items: Every hit you land writes your grade up from E to S; every hit you take strikes it out; it fades if you stop swinging.
Higher grade means more damage, faster cooldowns and more gold.
Runs end on an after-action ledger - grade attained, time, kills, damage, drops.

sections.heading: Enemies
items: Four enemy types plus elites, replacing the single one that walked at you: stalkers, swarms, wardens that telegraph a ground slam, and casters that lock a lane and fire down it.
Attacks are drawn on the floor before they land, and dashing through one as it resolves is a perfect parry - mana back, grade up, and the field slows.

sections.heading: Weapons and ultimates
items: Sixteen weapons with sixteen mechanics nobody else has - venom stacks you detonate, frost brands that shatter into neighbours, a blade that anchors and snaps back, a shield stance that returns what it absorbs, chains, pins, gravity in both directions, ice walls, and squares of the world you simply delete.
Twelve ultimates that are now twelve different events rather than one move in twelve costumes.

sections.heading: Also
items: Simulated fire that whips and sheds as you sweep it, and a new endgame S+ rift.
Stat points can be spent 5 or all at once. All 44 skill icons redrawn and now unique.
Channelled abilities no longer stall, and a crash on minimised windows is fixed.

entries.title: Port Vesper - Night Shift
entries.summary: A full engine rewrite and a substantial expansion, from roughly 2,500 to 6,200 lines.

sections.heading: Visuals
items: New layered renderer: cached ground chunks, a separate additive light buffer, and a post chain of grade, wet reflections, vignette and film grain. Everything used to be drawn in one flat pass.
Night-first art direction - sodium streetlight against cyan-black, with real pools of light and wet-road reflections.

Buildings have per-window lighting, roof furniture, parapets and neon signage; cars are tapered hulls with turning wheels, brake lights and visible crash damage; pedestrians have limbs and a walk cycle.
Weather, a day/night cycle, blood, scorch and skid decals, plus hitstop, trauma-based shake and muzzle light.

sections.heading: City
items: The uniform grid is gone - avenues and side streets differ in width, and blocks vary in size.
Five districts with distinct palettes, building heights and props: Financial, Old Quarter, Port Authority, Foundry Row and Vesper Heights.
A working harbour with piers, cranes and water you can drown a car in.

sections.heading: Gameplay
items: Four contacts with ordered job chains and unlockable perks, and six mission types: steal, deliver, wreck, wipe, escort and heist.
Three gangs with territory and hostility tracking.
Gunplay rebuilt with magazines, reloads, recoil and accuracy bloom, plus grenades and molotovs.
Vehicle upgrades and nitrous, chop-shop want lists, and buyable property with nightly income.
Police escalation: roadblocks at three stars, a helicopter with searchlight at four, SWAT at five. Dispatch broadcasts your car's description, so a respray breaks the match.
Rebuilt traffic AI, oriented vehicle collision, and save/continue support.

sections.heading: Interface
items: Redesigned HUD, minimap and city map, plus a contacts phone, dispatch radio log and kill feed.
Expanded procedural audio.

entries.title: Foil & Fortune - Second Print
entries.summary: A full rewrite of Shop Floor. Same premise, almost everything else new.

sections.heading: Cards
items: Cards are generated as SVG rather than drawn as flat panels, with procedural art seeded per card - sky, horizon, element sigil and foreground framing composed to fit whatever shape the frame gives them.
Five frame tiers: Standard, Retro, Extended Art, Borderless and Showcase.
Six Showcase frames, one per set, each with its own geometry rather than a recolour - Ember Seal, Tide Glass, Storybook, Constellation, Schematic and Deco.
Eight foil finishes built as reflectivity maps, so the pattern only appears where the light falls and tilting the card lights a different part of it.
Grading slabs, a five-step rarity ladder, and frame and finish rolled independently of rarity.

sections.heading: Gameplay
items: A live meta - set values drift daily and shift hard every third day, so buying cold and selling hot is the core lever.
Three things to do with a carton: shelf it, rip it, or vault it sealed to appreciate.
Pricing is a real decision, with a fair-value gauge and customers who walk out if you gouge.
Five customer archetypes with their own budgets, patience and targets, now with proper A* pathfinding.
Checkout minigame, display case, card grading, walk-in trade offers, Friday Night tournaments, staff, upgrades and shop expansion.
Four-minute days with an end-of-day ledger - rent, wages, upkeep, and eviction if you stay underwater.

sections.heading: Presentation
items: Rebuilt as a rain-lit night shop: warm lamp pools against a cold street, real lighting and depth sorting, and a living window with falling rain, traffic, pedestrians, lightning and droplets crawling down the glass.
New UI throughout, plus a nine-step tutorial.

entries.title: Elementalis - Update
entries.summary: Every element gets its own identity, the world is now randomly seeded, and a long list of fixes.

sections.heading: Visuals
items: Every element has its own projectile art, flight trail and impact effect. All 21 used to share one glowing diamond with the colour swapped.
18 distinct particle textures replace the single glow sprite used for everything.
Ground effects are drawn as what they are - lava pools crust over with glowing cracks, vines grow outward, the void rift reads as an actual hole.
Enemies carry physical elemental features instead of just being tinted, and each element has its own icon in the spell bar and Grimoire.
Added critical hits, and rebalanced screen shake so small hits got more punch and big spells no longer white out the screen.

sections.heading: Sound
items: All new and fully procedural, with no audio files: a distinct cast voice per element family plus hit, kill, hurt, blink, level-up and fusion sounds. Toggle in the top right.

sections.heading: Gameplay
items: Enemies telegraph their attacks with a wind-up ring, so ranged shots and boss attacks can be read and dodged.
Wardens have less health and mana regenerates a little faster.
Fusions are easier to reach, so third-circle elements and Ascendant are attainable in a normal run.
Clearing an enemy camp pays an essence bonus, and the compass points to the nearest shrine of an element you have not attuned yet.

sections.heading: World generation
items: The world is randomly seeded - every playthrough used to generate the identical map, shrines and starting position.
Shrine elements are evenly distributed rather than tied to biome, which had made Earth shrines overwhelmingly common and Fire and Arcane rare.
Shrines are guaranteed to be spaced apart, and your starting position varies between runs.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Fixed a hash overflow that was skewing terrain and site generation.
Boss attacks no longer continue firing while the Grimoire is open or after you die.
Holding Shift no longer chain-dashes, and the death screen no longer stacks on top of the Grimoire.
Fixed garbled characters in on-screen messages, and the HUD not updating live.

sections.heading: Performance
items: Terrain generation is spread across frames, removing the stutter when moving into new areas - roughly a 12ms spike per chunk down to 3ms.
Faster particle handling, cached gradients, and less per-frame work throughout.
Quality scaling under load only thins background ambience; spell effects, enemies and lighting are never reduced.

entries.title: Cosmic Climb v2.0
entries.summary: A complete rebuild. Same 3,000m climb, almost nothing else is the same.

sections.heading: New art direction
items: Rebuilt the whole look as a risograph screenprint: flat spot inks, visible plate misregistration, halftone dot screens, paper grain and corner trim marks, replacing the old pastel gradients and frosted glass.
Each of the 8 altitude bands is its own print run with a distinct two-ink palette. The Void inverts entirely - black stock, cream ink.
New parallax backdrop: ringed gas giants, halftone nebula tints, a black hole, drifting registration marks and cirrus streaks.
Redesigned player with a tapered motion trail, squash-and-stretch and lean.

sections.heading: New gameplay
items: Air dash - directional, refills on landing or stardust, and shatters debris you dash through.
The Collapse - a rising tide of black ink chases you up the page, replacing the old static death line. Standing still is fatal.
Stardust to Chain to Surge - collect dust to build a chain multiplier and charge Surge, a launch that shoves the ink back down the sheet.
Six platform types: solid slabs, drifting, crumbling, phasing, launch kickers and realm gates.
Hazards - tumbling debris and telegraphed pulsar sweeps in the upper realms.
Variable jump height, coyote time and input buffering.

sections.heading: New audio and interface
items: Full procedural soundtrack and SFX via WebAudio, with no audio files. Per-realm drone bed and a low rumble that rises as the ink closes in.
Printed instrument panels for altitude, score, dust, flow meter, dash pips and chain, plus a vertical altimeter tape.
Redesigned title, pause and run-summary cards with full run stats, and rebuilt touch controls.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Falling fast no longer drops you straight through platforms.
Altitude is now resolution-independent - it used to scale with window height.
The launch field has an actual floor instead of a bottomless pit.

entries.title: Neon Speed Simulator - September update
entries.summary: Saving fixed, the Wraith made beatable, and a faster, better-looking world.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Fixed saving. Progress on signed-in accounts was not being stored at all - levels, cores, upgrades and unlocked chassis now persist properly.

Fixed the Crimson Wraith. It was impossible to genuinely outrun, which made the APEX challenge uncompletable. It can now be escaped by committing to your boost, and surviving a full chase finally counts.
Fixed the game failing to load after the move to the new site.
Removed the hazard rocks, so open space is clear again at any speed.

sections.heading: Balance
items: Chassis unlock far sooner - the full roster tops out at 42 prestiges instead of 120, and the world-bending chassis arrive much earlier.
Boost lasts longer and recharges faster. It used to be unavailable for most of the early game.
Getting caught by the Wraith hurts less: a smaller core loss and a shorter penalty.

sections.heading: Visuals and performance
items: The Classic Interceptor has a proper engine trail - a plume with shock cells and vortex rings that builds as you accelerate.
Redesigned energy orbs with clearer tiers, and real feedback on collection.
Added depth behind the world, with the simulation's lattice receding into the distance.
Orb rendering is roughly 4x faster with no loss in quality.
